summary: A 1933 CCC-built Aermotor tower on a high Smokies summit, now an NPS radio repeater, nominally still climbable per its 2007 register listing.

facts.design: 60 ft steel Aermotor tower, 7 ft x 7 ft metal cab
facts.status_note: No longer staffed as a fire lookout; the National Park Service uses it as a radio repeater, and Wikipedia's mountain entry describes the tower as abandoned. No source gives a date for when fire-watching ended.

access.note: Reached by maintained NPS trails (Mount Sterling Trail, Mount Sterling Ridge Trail, Baxter Creek Trail) and no source calls the tower closed, but none states current public access or climbing rules either.

visit.trail_note: 2.7 mi one-way via Mount Sterling Trail from Mount Sterling Gap; also reachable via the 5.3 mi Mount Sterling Ridge Trail or the Baxter Creek Trail from Big Creek Campground.

facts.agency: Great Smoky Mountains National Park (National Park Service); administered by Haywood County, North Carolina per its NHLR listing

events.note: CCC-built, prefabricated Aermotor steel tower with 7x7 ft metal cab
Registered March 19, 2007 as US 689 / NC 10, nominated by Peter Barr

notes_for_editor: Beyond the NHLR register page, no newspaper or Forest Service archival material turned up for this specific tower in cached sources or three web searches; a 'Sterling Mountain' NRHP tower that surfaced in search results is a different structure in Orange County, New York, and was excluded. Wikipedia calling the tower 'abandoned' sits a little oddly next to NHLR's description of an open trap door and NPS radio-repeater use -- worth a direct check of current NPS trail/tower status pages. Current staffing and public-access level are inferred, not confirmed by an authoritative current source.
